You can mount an optic on a carry handle but the optic ends up being quite high up which is a bit of a nuisance at closer ranges. It still works but it's better to have your optic as close to the barrel as you can get it.

I find iron sights in general are more difficult to zero as opposed to red dots or scopes. It shouldn't be any more difficult to to zero the iron sights on a rail as opposed to iron sights on the gas block.

It's also advantageous to to have your front and rear sights farther apart from each other. It gives a longer sight radius which helps with accuracy. Having a gas block front sight limits you in that regard.

Longer rails also protect the barrel more which helps to maintain the accuracy of your AR by protecting the barrel from falls and what not.
